1.title: Architecture Models and Securing Infrastructure
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Architecture Models and Securing Infrastructure. It covers the exam area Security Architecture. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. three point one Compare and contrast security implications of different architecture models. three point two Given a scenario, manage the security architecture to best protect the infrastructure. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Security Architecture (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: Architecture and infrastructure models
1.text: Architecture and infrastructure models. Cloud. Meaning: Rented computing from a provider. Security point: Shared responsibility: the provider secures the platform, you secure data, identities and configuration. Serverless. Meaning: Code runs without managing servers. Security point: Less to patch, but permissions and code still matter. Multicloud. Meaning: Using more than one cloud provider. Security point: Avoids lock-in, adds complexity and more places to secure.

1.title: Architecture and infrastructure models, continued
1.text: Architecture and infrastructure models. Deployment models. Meaning: Public, private, hybrid (mix), community (shared by a group with common needs). Security point: More control in private, more flexibility in public. Infrastructure as code. Meaning: Infrastructure defined in files. Security point: Repeatable and reviewable; scan the code for mistakes. Operational technology (O T). Meaning: Industrial control systems. Security point: Long life, hard to patch: segment it. On-premises. Meaning: Your own datacenter. Security point: Full control, you carry all the cost and responsibility.

1.title: Architecture and infrastructure models, continued
1.text: Architecture and infrastructure models. Air-gapped network. Meaning: No connection to other networks. Security point: Strongest isolation; still at risk from removable media and insiders. Microservices. Meaning: An app split into small services. Security point: Smaller blast radius, but many A P Is to secure. Segmentation. Meaning: Logical (V L A Ns, subnets) or physical (separate hardware). Security point: Limits lateral movement.

1.title: Architecture and infrastructure models, continued
1.text: Architecture and infrastructure models. The figure shows this: Cloud shared responsibility and deployment models: public, private, hybrid, community.

1.title: Considerations when choosing
1.text: Considerations when choosing. Availability, resilience, proprietary versus open source, usability, responsibility, compute, power requirements, ease of recovery. Data sovereignty (laws of the data's location), data classification, cost, ownership, environmental requirements, scalability, risk. Exam tip: In the cloud, you always keep responsibility for your data, identities and configuration. Data sovereignty equals the country's laws apply to the data stored there. An air gap is isolation, not immunity.

1.title: Protecting the infrastructure
1.text: Protecting the infrastructure. Device placement. Put devices where they control traffic: firewall at the edge, sensors at choke points. Security zones. Group systems by trust: internal, D M Z (screened subnet for public servers), untrusted (internet), guest. Attack surface. Reduce it: close ports, remove services, limit exposure. Diversity. Use different vendors, platforms and controls so one flaw does not break everything. Failure modes. Fail open (stays available when it fails) versus fail closed (blocks when it fails: secure but can stop business).

1.title: Zero Trust architecture
1.text: Zero Trust architecture. Zero Trust removes implicit trust. Elements in the objectives. User authentication: strong, continuous verification. Device management: device health (is it patched and compliant?) and inventory. Application access control: access to each application, not the whole network. Control plane versus data plane: policy decisions are made in the control plane and enforced in the data plane.

1.title: Secure communication and access
1.text: Secure communication and access. V P N (virtual private network), remote access, tunneling. Encrypted paths for remote users and sites. User management and least privilege. Only the needed access. End-to-end encrypted messaging. Only the sender and receiver can read. Out-of-band management. Manage devices over a separate, protected path. File transfer. Use secure protocols (S F T P, F T P S) instead of plain F T P. Security Service Edge (S S E). Cloud-delivered security (web gateway, Z T N A, cloud access broker) for users anywhere.

1.title: Identity management
1.text: Identity management. Group managed service accounts (G M S As) give services automatically managed passwords. Use least privilege access accounts. Watch privilege creep: users collecting rights as they change roles. Exam tip: A screened subnet (D M Z) holds public-facing servers between two firewalls. Fail closed protects security; fail open protects availability (for example a fire exit door). Privilege creep is solved by access reviews. Exam tip: Segmentation limits lateral movement, and Zero Trust removes trust based on location: both reduce the blast radius of a breach.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors hosts its public web servers in a separate network between two firewalls. What is this network called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Screened subnet (D M Z). A screened subnet or D M Z holds public-facing servers, separated from the internal network.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A factory control network must have no connection to any other network. Which design fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Air-gapped network. An air-gapped network has no connection to other networks.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company stores customer data in a cloud region in another country and worries about local laws. Which concept applies? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Data sovereignty. Data sovereignty means the data is subject to the laws of the country where it is stored.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A door controller fails and the door locks everyone out to protect the room. Which failure mode is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Fail closed. The system defaults to a secure, blocking state, which is fail closed.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Administrators manage network switches over a dedicated protected network separate from production traffic. What is this called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Out-of-band management. Managing devices over a separate path from the data network is out-of-band management.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Users move between teams and keep all their old permissions. Which problem is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Privilege creep. Accumulating permissions as roles change is privilege creep.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the four cloud deployment models. Answer: Public, private, hybrid and community. Question two. What does I A C stand for? Answer: Infrastructure as code. Question three. What is the purpose of segmentation? Answer: To limit lateral movement and contain damage.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between fail open and fail closed? Answer: Fail open stays available when it fails; fail closed blocks to stay secure. Question five. What does S S E provide? Answer: Cloud-delivered security services such as a web gateway and Zero Trust network access. Question six. What is a G M S A? Answer: A group managed service account with automatically managed passwords.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Models: cloud (shared responsibility), serverless, multicloud, public or private or hybrid or community, I A C, O T, on-premises, air-gapped, microservices. Choosing: availability, resilience, usability, ease of recovery; data sovereignty, classification, cost, scalability, risk. Protect: device placement, security zones (D M Z), reduce attack surface, diversity, fail open versus closed. Zero Trust: verify users and devices (health, inventory), per-application access. Access: V P N, tunneling, end to end messaging, out-of-band management, secure file transfer, S S E. In the next module, we continue the course.
